and so she was, no doubt, physically speaking. But then there was an expression of almost
insupportable haughtiness in her bearing and countenance. She had Roman features and a
double chin, disappearing into a throat like a pillar. These features appeared to me not
only inflated and darkened, but even furrowed with pride. And the chin was sustained by

a fierce and a hard eye. It reminded me of Mrs. Reed's. She mouthed her words in speaking,
her voice was deep, its inflections very pompous, very dogmatical, very intolerable in short.
